Show path outline arc_path = Arc(radius=axes.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2) arc_path.move_to(axes.c2p(0,0)) self.play(Create(arc_path)) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 === self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW) # Track rotation angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0) dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())))) self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear) dot.clear_updaters() self.wait(0.5) # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 === self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW) # Landing pulse effect pulse = Circle(radius=0.1, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4).move_to(axes.c2p(-1, 0)) self.add(pulse) self.play( pulse.animate.scale(5).set_stroke(opacity=0), FadeIn(formula_1, shift=UP), run_time=1.5 ) self.remove(pulse) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 === self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW) # Transform formula self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(formula_1, formula_final)) self.play(formula_final.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=1) self.wait(3) from manim import * import numpy as np class TeachingScene(Scene): def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines): # BASE self.camera.background_color = "#000000" self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP) self.add(self.title) # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-") lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines] self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8) self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2) self.add(self.lecture) # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side) self.grid = {} rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"] # Top to bottom cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"] # Left to right for i, row in enumerate(rows): for j, col in enumerate(cols): x = 0.5 + j * 1 y = 2.2 - i * 1 self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0]) def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0): mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos]) return mobject def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0): tl_pos = self.grid[top_left] br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right] # Calculate center of the area center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2 center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2 center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0]) mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(center) return mobject class Section7Scene(TeachingScene): def construct(self): # Setup layout lecture_lines = [ 'This formula powers modern physics and engineering.', 'It describes waves, electricity, and quantum mechanics.', 'A simple circle explains the harmony of our universe.' ] self.setup_layout("Real-World Echoes", lecture_lines) # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 === # Colors COLOR_VEC = YELLOW COLOR_WAVE = "#55FFFF" COLOR_ICON = WHITE # Grid locations plane_center = self.grid["D2"] wave_start_x = self.grid["D3"][0] wave_end_x = self.grid["D6"][0] # Time tracking time_tracker = ValueTracker(0) drawing_tracker = ValueTracker(0) # Progress of the sine wave trace (0 to width) # Complex Plane Elements circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE) circle.move_to(plane_center) h_axis_plane = Line(plane_center + LEFT*1.0, plane_center + RIGHT*1.0, color=GRAY, stroke_width=1) v_axis_plane = Line(plane_center + DOWN*1.0, plane_center + UP*1.0, color=GRAY, stroke_width=1) # Rotating Vector and Dot # Using persistent mobjects with updaters vector = Line(plane_center, plane_center + RIGHT*0.8, color=COLOR_VEC) vector.add_updater(lambda v: v.set_angle(time_tracker.get_value())) dot_on_circle = Dot(color=COLOR_VEC, radius=0.06) dot_on_circle.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(vector.get_end())) # Display elements self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_VEC) self.play( Create(h_axis_plane), Create(v_axis_plane), Create(circle), Create(vector), FadeIn(dot_on_circle) ) self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(TAU), run_time=2, rate_func=linear) # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 === # Time Axis for Sine Wave time_axis = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D6"], color=GRAY, stroke_width=1) # Horizontal trace connection (Dashed line) connection_line = DashedLine( dot_on_circle.get_center(), [wave_start_x, dot_on_circle.get_center()[1], 0], color=GRAY, dash_length=0.05, stroke_opacity=0.6 ) connection_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on( dot_on_circle.get_center(), [wave_start_x, dot_on_circle.get_center()[1], 0] )) # Sine wave via ParametricFunction (efficient for scrolling) freq = 3.0 sine_wave = always_redraw(lambda: ParametricFunction( lambda x: np.array([ x, plane_center[1] + 0.8 * np.sin(time_tracker.get_value() - freq * (x - wave_start_x)), 0 ]), t_range=[wave_start_x, wave_start_x + drawing_tracker.get_value()], color=COLOR_WAVE )) self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_WAVE) self.play(Create(time_axis), Create(connection_line), Create(sine_wave)) # Grow wave trace and continue rotation self.play( drawing_tracker.animate.set_value(wave_end_x - wave_start_x), time_tracker.animate.increment_value(2*TAU), run_time=4, rate_func=linear ) # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 === # Application Icons # Signal Tower Icon tower_base = Triangle(color=COLOR_ICON).scale(0.15) tower_pole = Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.4, color=COLOR_ICON).next_to(tower_base, UP, buff=0) tower_wave1 = Arc(radius=0.1, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI/2, color=COLOR_ICON).move_to(tower_pole.get_top() + UP*0.1) tower_wave2 = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI/2, color=COLOR_ICON).move_to(tower_pole.get_top() + UP*0.2) tower = VGroup(tower_base, tower_pole, tower_wave1, tower_wave2) self.place_at_grid(tower, "B5", scale_factor=0.8) # Musical Note Icon note_head = Dot(color=COLOR_ICON, radius=0.1) note_stem = Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=COLOR_ICON).move_to(note_head.get_right() + UP*0.2) note_flag = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.3 + DOWN*0.15, color=COLOR_ICON).move_to(note_stem.get_top() + RIGHT*0.15 + DOWN*0.07) musical_note = VGroup(note_head, note_stem, note_flag) self.place_at_grid(musical_note, "B6", scale_factor=0.8) self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) self.play( FadeIn(tower, shift=UP*0.3), FadeIn(musical_note, shift=UP*0.3) ) # Final rotation loop to wrap up self.play(time_tracker.animate.increment_value(3*TAU), run_time=5, rate_func=linear) self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Most Beautiful Equation: Visualizing Euler's Identity
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or early university students with a basic interest in math and physics.

sections.title: The Cosmic Reunion
sections.content: Introduction to the equation e^{iπ} + 1 = 0. Briefly explain why it is considered the 'most beautiful'—it unites five fundamental mathematical constants (0, 1, e, i, and π) in a single, simple relationship.
sections.example: Visualize five diverse characters representing 0 (The Void), 1 (The Unit), e (The Growth), i (The Rotation), and π (The Circle) receiving an invitation to a grand gala.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The 2D Playground
sections.content: Introduce the Complex Plane. Explain that while real numbers live on a horizontal line, 'i' introduces a vertical dimension. Crucial concept: multiplying by 'i' is equivalent to a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.
sections.example: A small robot walking along the x-axis. When it hits an 'i' power-up, it rotates 90 degrees to face North (the imaginary axis) instead of walking further East.

sections.title: The Engine of Growth (Understanding 'e')
sections.content: Define 'e' (approx. 2.718) as the base of continuous growth. Usually, e^x means growing 'outward' faster and faster. Establish that 'e' is the math of 'change based on current state'.
sections.example: A magical plant that grows at a rate proportional to its current height; the more it grows, the faster it continues to grow.

sections.title: The Sideways Push (The i-Exponent)
sections.content: Explain what happens when the growth rate is 'i'. Since 'i' rotates things by 90 degrees, the growth isn't 'outward' (larger), but 'sideways' (perpendicular to the current position). This sideways push creates a circle.
sections.example: A planet orbiting a sun. Gravity pulls it, but its velocity is sideways. In Euler's formula, 'i' acts like a steering wheel constantly turning the growth vector into a perfect circular path.

sections.title: The Journey of π Radians
sections.content: Introduce π as the distance of the journey. If e^{iθ} traces a circle, then θ is the distance traveled along the edge. Since a full circle is 2π, a distance of π is exactly half a circle.
sections.example: An ant walking along the edge of a unit circle starting at position (1,0). It travels a distance of π (3.14 units), tracing a 180-degree arc.

sections.title: The Grand Destination: e^{iπ} = -1
sections.content: Combine all elements. Starting at 1 on the real axis, the 'i' exponent rotates our path into a circle, and the 'π' tells us to go halfway around. We land exactly at -1 on the real axis.
sections.example: An animation showing a point starting at 1, curving smoothly around the origin like a swinging pendulum, and stopping exactly at -1, proving e^{iπ} + 1 = 0.

sections.title: Real-World Echoes
sections.content: Wrap up by explaining that this isn't just a party trick; it's the foundation of how we describe waves, alternating current in electronics, and quantum mechanics.
sections.example: Show a spinning wheel (Euler's rotation) being projected onto a wall to create a sine wave, linking the formula to music and radio signals.

storyboard.title: The Cosmic Reunion
lecture_lines: This is the most beautiful equation in mathematics.
It unites five fundamental constants in one simple line.
Zero, one, e, i, and pi join together.
From the void of zero to the growth of e.
All connected in a single, elegant relationship.
animations: Display the full equation $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ in the center of the screen (#FFFFFF).
Apply distinct colors to each constant: $e$ (#55FF55), $i$ (#5555FF), $\pi$ (#FF5555), $1$ (#FFFFFF), and $0$ (#AAAAAA).
Scale up the constant 'e' (#55FF55) and show a brief growth pulse effect.
Scale up 'i' (#5555FF) and '\pi' (#FF5555) as they glow and slightly vibrate in the exponent.
Highlight the entire equation with a soft golden glow (#FFFF88) to emphasize the unity of these constants.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The 2D Playground
lecture_lines: Real numbers live on a flat horizontal line.
The imaginary unit i adds a vertical dimension.
Multiplying by i creates a ninety-degree turn.
animations: Draw a horizontal real axis (#FFFFFF) and a vertical imaginary axis (#5555FF) crossing at the origin, with the ground [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ground.svg] providing a baseline for the horizontal axis.
Place a point at 1 on the real axis and label it '1' (#FFFFFF).
Animate the point at 1 rotating 90 degrees counter-clockwise to the position 'i' (#5555FF) on the imaginary axis.

storyboard.title: The Engine of Growth (Understanding 'e')
lecture_lines: e is the base of continuous, natural growth.
Growth happens faster as the value increases.
It represents change based on its current state.
animations: Display the letter 'e' (#55FF55) and the value '2.718...' directly below it.
Animate a line graph starting at (0,1) that curves upward sharply to demonstrate exponential growth.
Flash the word 'GROWTH' (#55FF55) alongside the engine icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/engine.svg] in bold text next to the steepest part of the curve.

storyboard.title: The Sideways Push (The i-Exponent)
lecture_lines: What happens if our growth rate is imaginary?
The imaginary unit i pushes growth sideways.
Instead of growing outward, the path begins to curve.
This constant perpendicular push forms a perfect circle.
It acts like a steering wheel for growth.
animations: Show a vector (#FFFFFF) pointing from the origin to 1 on the real axis in the complex plane.
Introduce 'i' into the exponent of 'e'; the growth vector turns 90 degrees to point toward the imaginary axis.
As the exponent grows, the vector's tip traces a smooth circular path (#FF5555).
Show a small perpendicular force arrow (#5555FF) at the tip of the vector, illustrating the 'sideways' push.
Label the resulting path as 'Circular Motion' (#FFFFFF) around the origin.

storyboard.title: The Journey of π Radians
lecture_lines: In Euler's formula, the exponent is the distance traveled.
A full trip around is two pi radians.
Traveling exactly pi takes us halfway around.
animations: Show a unit circle (#AAAAAA) on the complex plane with a starting point at (1,0).
Trace a red arc (#FF5555) counter-clockwise along the circle's perimeter starting from (1,0).
The arc stops exactly halfway around the circle at the point (-1,0), and the label '\pi' (#FF5555) appears.

storyboard.title: The Grand Destination: e^{iπ} = -1
lecture_lines: We start at one on the real axis.
The i exponent turns our path into a circle.
We travel a distance of exactly pi.
This journey lands us perfectly at negative one.
Add one, and we arrive back at zero.
animations: Start with the point at 1 on the real axis in the complex plane.
Animate the point traveling along the circular path for a total distance of \pi radians.
The point lands precisely on -1 on the real axis, which is highlighted with a pulse effect.
Display the resulting formula $e^{i\pi} = -1$ in large, bold text (#FFFFFF) above the axes.
Shift the -1 to the left side of the equation to reveal the final form: $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$.

lecture_lines: This formula powers modern physics and engineering.
It describes waves, electricity, and quantum mechanics.
A simple circle explains the harmony of our universe.
animations: Display the rotating vector in the complex plane alongside a scrolling time-axis.
Trace the vertical component of the rotation to draw a continuous Sine Wave (#55FFFF).

Show small icons of a signal tower [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg] (#FFFFFF) and a musical note [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/note.svg] (#FFFFFF) to represent waves and vibrations.
